rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~97% 25bp / ~3% 50bp (CME FedWatch via Hercules); ECB Dec ~90%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec second hike ~70–75%; BoC Dec ~44%; Fed minutes Wed Nov 18 1:00 PM CT
rows.read: A December Fed rate hike is still seen as all but certain, and New York Fed President John Williams said one more is probably needed, but nothing dramatic. Europe, Britain and Japan are also expected to hike, while Canada and New Zealand look more likely to wait. US rates still look set to rise fastest, which keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Japan exports Oct +20.5% y/y, a monthly record; US retail sales Oct +0.2% m/m (fcst +0.1%); NAHB builder index 25, lowest since April 2012
rows.read: Japan's exports hit a record in October on chip demand, a sign its economy is picking up after a small summer dip. In the US, shoppers keep spending while housing struggles. The US still looks firmer than most, which supports the dollar.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: UK CPI Oct 3.6% y/y (fcst 3.6%), core 2.8%, services 3.7% (ONS); Australia wage price index Q3 +1.1% q/q (fcst +1.0%), +3.5% y/y (ABS); euro-area final CPI Oct due 4:00 AM CT (fcst 4.0%)
rows.read: UK inflation rose to 3.6% as expected, pushed up by fuel, while core prices stayed steady, so the pound got no new lift. Australian pay rose a bit faster than forecast, keeping alive the case for another rate hike there. Inflation is still well above target almost everywhere, which keeps most central banks leaning toward hikes.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: Markets stayed nervous, with US stocks down for a second day and Iran attacking Bahrain again. Gold fell instead of rising, as some investors sold it to raise cash. The dollar gained from the unease, while the Aussie and kiwi, which track market mood, slipped.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.read: Oil fell as US crude stocks rose, which takes a little away from the Canadian dollar. Gold's slide below $3,800 weighs on the Aussie, since Australia is a big gold producer. Cheaper oil helps importers such as the euro area and Japan.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC report of Nov 10 (out late after Veterans Day): hedge funds for USD, GBP, AUD and gold; against EUR, NZD, CAD and CHF; slightly against JPY; real money disagrees on EUR, GBP and AUD
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds leaning toward the dollar and the pound and against the euro, the kiwi and the Canadian dollar, with bets against the kiwi growing fastest. Big long-term investors take the other side on the euro, pound and Aussie. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.09% in Asian trading (Hercules)
rows.read: Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs above 5%, which weighs a little on trust in the dollar. France's debt troubles keep weighing on the euro.
